name: Grow mushrooms
blurb: Oyster mushrooms on a kit or on inoculated logs, indoors and out of season. Fast, surprising, and completely different from growing plants.
gear: A mushroom kit, or spawn plus a substrate
Somewhere humid and out of direct sun
steps: Start with a ready-made kit to learn the cycle before attempting your own substrate.
Learn the two phases: colonisation, where the mycelium takes over the substrate in the dark, then fruiting, triggered by light, air and humidity.
Keep humidity high during fruiting by misting several times a day, without soaking the substrate.
Give good fresh airflow — mushrooms with long thin stems and tiny caps are short of air.
Harvest just before the caps flatten and the edges turn up.
Soak the block and try for a second and third flush, then compost it.
tips: Green or black mould means contamination. Discard it rather than trying to rescue it.
Only ever eat mushrooms you grew from known spawn. This is not a route into wild foraging.
proof: Two flushes of mushrooms you grew and cooked.
